name: kanbanly
overview: Self-hosted, multi-project kanban board whose data lives in git repositories as markdown files. Coding agents create cards, move them, and write human-readable status narratives as they work. A hosted SaaS offers the same product managed, with S3 storage, an AI assistant, and one-click export back to git.
problemStatement: Coding agents do substantial work but leave no durable, human-legible record of what they did, what they're doing, or what they discovered. Existing trackers are SaaS-only, API-driven, and hostile to agents that are good at editing files and running git. kanbanly makes the tracker a git repo of markdown.
corePrinciple: Git is the only contract. The UI and the coding agent are independent clients of the same remote — no API between them, no auth between them, neither needs to know the other exists.

inScope: Card format: markdown + YAML frontmatter, ## Status / ## Log conventions
Boards stored in dedicated git repo(s), addressed as (remote, path)
Two layouts: one boards repo with directory per board, or one repo per board
.kanbanly.yml pointer committed in the code repo
@kanbanly/core shared package: Zod schema, ID/order rules, merge driver, storage adapters
Custom git merge driver with designed conflict-marker fallback
OSS server: connect boards repo, render, drag-and-drop, card edit, quick-add, archive
Optimistic UI -> local commit -> background push queue
Installable setup skill + in-repo AGENTS.md conventions
Filter bar, keyboard navigation, board activity feed
outOfScope: Real-time multiplayer presence, cursors, CRDT co-editing
Enterprise self-deploy of the SaaS stack
postMvpRoadmap: One-way GitHub Issues import; two-way Issues sync

stack.runtime: Bun (npm package must stay Node-compatible best-effort for npx users)
stack.frontend: TanStack Start (full-stack) + Router + Query + Table + Form
stack.distribution: Docker + npm only; no standalone binary
stack.requires: git in $PATH (server shells out to real git CLI)

packages.packages/core: @kanbanly/core — card schema (zod), id + order-key rules, merge driver, storage adapters (git | s3), ai tool definitions

closed.adds: tenants, auth, billing, AI service, portfolio view

body.## Status: overwritten on every state change — the now

ordering.agentRule: read target column, take largest order, mint after it — never insert between

writePaths.humanUI: server writes on their behalf, always to default branch
writePaths.note: separate clones synced through the remote; ~15s worst-case propagation accepted

credentials.agent: developer's existing SSH agent or git credential helper — zero kanbanly-specific setup
credentials.server: ~/.kanbanly/creds.age (0600) encrypted with ~/.kanbanly/key (0600), or mounted SSH key

conflictResolution.pushRetry: git pull --rebase then re-push, up to 3 attempts
conflictResolution.installation: per-clone via git config — git does not let a repo define what a driver executes
conflictResolution.fallback: clone without driver produces conflict markers; server detects on fetch, heals with same logic, commits
conflictResolution.hazard: plain merge=union on YAML frontmatter produces duplicate keys silently resolved to the last value — silent data loss

serverState.index: in-memory index[remote] = { sha, boards, cards }, rebuilt only on SHA change

saas.cardStorage: S3, one object per card, git-identical format, ETag If-Match compare-and-swap, bucket versioning on
saas.relationalStorage: Postgres — tenants, users, auth, billing, chat history, audit log
saas.mergeDriver: unnecessary in SaaS — conditional writes replace it
saas.auth: device-code login; credential never passes through the agent or transcript

aiTools.writePolicy: all writes require an in-chat confirm chip before committing

saas.export: one-click push to my GitHub materializes S3 into a real git repo, plus downloadable .bundle
saas.deployment: Helm chart + Compose file, operated by us; Postgres via CloudNativePG in-cluster or external URL

userExperience.visualDirection: Clean, calm product identity — no mascot. Muted palette, strong typography, generous whitespace.
userExperience.theme: Light / Dark / System switch, persisted per browser, defaults to system preference. Both themes first-class, WCAG AA.
errorStates: Credential invalid/expired/missing scopes -> banner naming the missing scope + re-enter flow
Offline / remote unreachable -> local commits work, pushes queue, 'offline — N changes pending', drains on reconnect
Malformed frontmatter -> quarantine lane with parse error; board still renders
Unknown column id -> quarantine lane with one-click 'move all to ->' picker; nothing auto-moves
Unresolvable conflict after 3 attempts -> freeze sync, show both sides, keep-mine / keep-theirs

securityPosture.authentication: none in OSS, by explicit decision
securityPosture.hostOverride: --host prints a loud warning that anyone reachable can push to connected repos
securityPosture.acceptedRisk: an exposed no-auth instance hands push access to anyone on the network
securityPosture.telemetry: none by default; optional check_updates hits GitHub releases API only

phases.name: Format & Skill
phases.rationale: The file format is the contract everything depends on and can be fully specified and tested with zero server code.

verificationLayers: Tests against real temp git repos — git init in a temp dir, drive real conflicts. Git is not mocked.
Merge-driver conflict fixtures — two-sided card edits with expected merged output. Guards the duplicate-YAML-key hazard.
Playwright end-to-end drag test — real browser drag, assert card lands AND commit exists.
Skill conformance test — real agent against a fixture boards repo, assert schema-valid cards with correct IDs and order keys.
openConcerns: The frontmatter merge driver is the highest-risk component. Plain merge=union on YAML produces duplicate keys that parsers silently resolve to the last one — silent data loss. Write the fixture table before the driver.
Git's merge-driver security model means .gitattributes alone is not enough. The driver command must be installed per-clone via git config. The conflict-healing fallback is not optional.
Pragmatic drag-and-drop uses native HTML5 drag events, notoriously fiddly to drive in Playwright. Pin the e2e drag test down early.
Bun is the runtime but npx users land on Node. Both need testing per release.
OSS has no authentication by explicit decision. The 127.0.0.1 default and the --host warning are the only mitigations; do not weaken either.
Agents sharing a checkout can race on a card file. Documented as a known limit with a re-read-before-write convention.
@kanbanly/core is the AGPL boundary. Anything the closed SaaS repo needs must live there; anything SaaS-specific must not leak into it.
